title: agent/1 — the discovery document at /.well-known/agent
pitch: agent/1 is the vendor-neutral discovery document at /.well-known/agent through which a website, API or company exposes an authenticated, discoverable, payable machine interface to agents — and through which agents find one.

refusals.title: Capabilities are verbs
refusals.body: quote, book, refund — never sales, support, finance. A department tells an agent who to talk to; an action tells it what it can do. The id rule is a lower-case verb plus a denylist of eight department words, refused by name rather than by taste.

refusals.title: Endpoints stay on the organisation's own domain
refusals.body: Every endpoint's host must be the document's domain or a subdomain of it — never a parent, a sibling or a stranger. A document may not point agents at another company's endpoints, whatever the arrangement between them; the other company publishes its own document.

refusals.title: Prices are whole minor units with a currency
refusals.body: An amount of 2500 with a currency of GBP is twenty-five pounds. A float is refused, a bare number is refused, an amount with no currency is refused, and a price with no way to pay is refused.

refusals.title: An accountable human is required
refusals.body: A name and a mailbox somebody reads. The template placeholder is refused. An interface nobody answers for is one nobody can be asked to stop.

refusals.title: The checker refuses; it does not guess
refusals.body: Unknown keys are refused unless x- prefixed. Each refusal has a vector named for it, and the suite asserts every vector fails for exactly its rule and no other.

faq.a: A capability id that is a department word rather than a verb; an endpoint on a domain other than the document's own or a subdomain of it; a float price, a bare number, or a price with no payment method; a missing accountable human or the template placeholder; and unknown keys that are not x- prefixed. Every refusal has a vector named for it.

faq.q: Where does this sit in Web 4?
faq.a: The gateway layer — 'how do I connect to the old web?'. A human sees company.com; an agent fetches one file and learns who is accountable, what it may do, where each action lives, what it costs and how to pay. The stack page and the Web 4 hub show where it sits among the nine layers.

No. agent/1 is draft. No organisation outside the repositories that wrote it has been verified serving a document, and that number is printed rather than rounded up; the first independent adopter is the gate before the word standard.

faq.q: How is a document located from a domain?
faq.a: By agent-dns/1: one DNS TXT record at _agent.<domain> points at the domain's agent/1 document. DNS points; the document describes. agent-dns/1 is a sibling spec and is not redefined here.

faq.q: Why are prices whole minor units?
faq.a: Because a float is where money quietly loses a penny. An amount of 2500 in GBP is twenty-five pounds with no rounding to argue about, and a price with no way to pay is refused as useless to the agent reading it.

faq.q: Is the gateway service part of this repository?
faq.a: No. This is the open protocol half — the format, schema, checker and vectors. A commercial service that fronts sites which publish nothing is a separate repository and is never named here; the format is brand-neutral by rule, and a lint enforces it.
